lede: Markets drift into a US half-day session with a December Fed hike almost fully priced after hot PCE and GDP data. Gold holds near $3,575 above Wednesday's one-year low, Brent pushed toward $97 on Gulf supply attacks, and bitcoin hovers around $60K.
snapshot_time: 07:00 TRT gold · FX & Brent 26 Nov close · S&P 25 Nov

focus.text: Steadying near 3,575 after Wednesday's dip to 3,426 as near-certain Fed hike pricing caps rebounds. Sits just above its 3,573 pivot; thin US half-day liquidity is today's main risk.
Flat around 1.097 as Thanksgiving drained volume, hugging its 50-period average below 1.10. France and Spain flash CPI and S&P's France rating review are today's risks.

technicals.indicators: RSI(14, H1) ≈ 54 · daily pivot 3,573.1 · lower highs since mid-November
technicals.note: A run of lower highs since mid-month is forming a falling wedge on the 4-hour chart, with buyers active around 3,500 and the 3,426 one-year low.

technicals.indicators: Price at the 50-period MA (≈1.0970) · capped below the 1.10 handle
technicals.note: The pair is coiling between 1.0935 and 1.1025, with the 50-period average acting as the midpoint in holiday trade.
A 'death cross' has formed as the falling 50-day average slipped under the 200-day; the 58,525 June closing low is the level analysts watch on a daily close.
Ether trades near its 1,690 pivot after rebounding from last week's low near 1,544, still about 39% below its September high.
Solana remains inside a falling channel whose upper line sits near 78.50, testing support close to its July lows.

news.text: Futures price a December Fed hike at roughly 99% after October core PCE hit 3.3% and Q3 GDP was revised to 4.3%; the FOMC blackout starts Saturday.
Brent settled at $96.57 (+2.07%), a third straight gain, after Houthi strikes on Saudi refineries and reports of tankers hitting mines near Hormuz.
Ministers meet Sunday; delegates told Reuters the group may keep output targets unchanged through at least Q1 2027, while Iraq disputes its capacity estimate.
Tokyo core inflation rose to 2.9% but missed the 3.0% forecast, leaving USD/JPY near 159.35; Tokyo warned against one-sided moves, with 160 seen as the intervention zone.
European equities rallied on Thursday — DAX +2.1%, Stoxx 600 +1.75% — while Wall Street reopens today for a shortened session.
US spot bitcoin ETFs shed $453M on Wednesday, a seventh outflow day, taking November redemptions to a record $5.39B; ether funds lost $68.5M.
Around $7B of bitcoin options expire on Deribit at 11:00 TRT today, alongside CME's November futures, which can add volatility in thin trade.
Dollar stablecoin supply has fallen about $14.75B this month, the steepest monthly drop since mid-2022, signalling liquidity leaving the sector.
XRP and Solana led modest gains over the past day; Franklin's crypto index ETF is set to add HYPE on 1 Dec, and an FF unlock lands Sunday.
Spain moved to let its financial-intelligence unit freeze crypto accounts without a court order, while Japan's FSA is studying DeFi curbs.
The Fear & Greed index sits at 11–12, extreme fear; Galaxy withdrew its earlier bottom call for bitcoin.
